terra.problem: The joke makes the speed of the LORD’s answer its punchline. Humor must not target God or His words.
Bethlehem being David’s hometown is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Calling Keilah a real town is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The kitchen GPS joke does not make sense in the comparison.
Identifying Jesse as David’s father is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The cited verse does not establish that Samuel anointed David years ago. The passage also does not say whether Samuel was part of the move; it simply does not name him.
David’s having done his best baking is invented, as is the claim that he has been in the Lord’s will the whole time.
Papa puts himself into the Bible event by saying he would have tried to hand over a cookie.
The passage does not say David acted right away after hearing the news.
The spice-jar joke mentions a food ingredient outside the allowed cookie-making foods.
Papa calls Judah the “wrong place” in response to the baker’s answer. He never says “wrong” about an answer.
Calling Moab a neighboring land is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Counting a stretch of years on one batch of cookies is an unclear comparison, so the joke does not land.
